On 2023-05-22, the user was working on a research-project abstract about assessing procedural skills in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery and asked for help shortening it to 250 words.

The user's research project proposes using passive stereo imaging and a locally connected convolutional neural network to infer patient-side surgical manipulator kinematics from left and right endoscopic views, then relate robot pose over an operation to the operator's skill level. The project aims to provide consistent, quantitative, automated performance feedback, in contrast to time-consuming and potentially biased subjective assessments by senior surgeons.

The user's proposed kinematics model uses VGG19 as a pretrained base with trainable locally connected two-dimensional layers, concatenation, flattening, and 5% dropout to estimate binocular spatial positions of the two surgical tools. It minimizes Euclidean-distance loss against ground-truth positions recorded by the surgical robot. The work uses the three standard surgical tasks in the JIGSAWS dataset; the user reported kinematics-estimation correlation error below 8 millimeters across both robot arms for all three training tasks.

The revised draft described a study of robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery that uses passive stereo imaging and machine learning to assess robot-surgeon operators’ skill, addressing limited haptic feedback and subjective performance assessment.

The revised academic draft described a locally connected convolutional neural network using a pretrained VGG19 base and left and right endoscopic views as inputs.
